user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm Git hosting destination (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)
- [ ] Ensure you have admin access to both SVN and Git servers
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

```bash
# Backup SVN repo
svnadmin dump /path/to/svn/repo > svn_backup.dump
```

---

## Morning: Preparation (2–3 hours)

### 1. Install Required Tools
```bash
# macOS
brew install git git-svn svn

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install git git-svn subversion

# Verify
git svn --version
```

### 2. Build Authors File
Map SVN usernames → Git identities (required for commit history).

```bash
# Extract all SVN authors automatically
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet \
  | grep "^r" \
  | awk '{print $3}' \
  | sort -u > authors.txt
```

Edit `authors.txt` into this format:
```
jsmith = John Smith <john.smith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mary.jones@company.com>
(no author) = Legacy User <legacy@company.com>
```

### 3. Identify Your SVN Layout

| Layout Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Standard** | Has `/trunk`, `/branches`, `/tags` |
| **Non-standard** | Custom folder structure |

```bash
# Inspect structure
svn ls svn://your-repo-url
```

---

## Midday: Migration (2–4 hours)

### 4. Clone SVN → Git

**Standard layout:**
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors.txt \
  my-new-git-repo
```

**Non-standard layout:**
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --trunk=trunk \
  --branches=branches \
  --tags=releases \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  my-new-git-repo
```

> ⏱️ **Time varies** — expect ~1 min per 1,000 revisions

### 5. Convert SVN Branches & Tags
```bash
cd my-new-git-repo

# Convert remote SVN branches to local Git branches
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v "tags/" | grep -v "trunk"); do
  git branch "${branch##*/}" "refs/remotes/$branch"
done

# Convert SVN tags to proper Git tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep "tags/"); do
  git tag "${tag##*/tags/}" "$tag"
  git branch -d -r "$tag"
done
```

### 6. Clean Up
```bash
# Remove git-svn tracking references
git branch -d -r trunk
git remote rm origin  # removes svn remote if present

# Verify history looks correct
git log --oneline --graph --all | head -30
```

---

## Afternoon: Validation & Push (1–2 hours)

### 7. Validate Migration

```bash
# Compare commit counts
svn log svn://your-repo-url | grep "^r" | wc -l
git log --oneline | wc -l

# Spot-check specific commits
git log --all --oneline

# Verify branches
git branch -a

# Verify tags
git tag -l
```

### 8. Push to Remote Git Host
```bash
# Add your new Git remote
git remote add origin git@github.com:yourorg/your-repo.git

# Push everything
git push origin --all      # all branches
git push origin --tags     # all tags
```

---

## Late Afternoon: Team Cutover (1 hour)

### 9. Team Instructions
Send this to every developer:

```bash
# Each developer runs this — DO NOT migrate their local SVN working copy
git clone git@github.com:yourorg/your-repo.git
cd your-repo

# Set identity if not globally configured
git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "you@company.com"
```

### 10. Lock Down SVN
- Set SVN repo to **read-only** (don't delete it yet)
- Update CI/CD pipelines to point to Git
- Update any documentation, wikis, README links

```bash
# Example: make SVN read-only via hook
echo "#!/bin/sh
echo 'SVN is read-only. Use Git.' >&2
exit 1" > /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
chmod +x /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
```

---

## End of Day: Sign-Off Checklist

| Task | Done? |
|---|---|
| Full commit history preserved | ☐ |
| All branches migrated | ☐ |
| All tags migrated | ☐ |
| Authors correctly mapped | ☐ |
| CI/CD updated | ☐ |
| Team successfully cloned | ☐ |
| SVN set to read-only | ☐ |
| SVN backup stored safely | ☐ |

---

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Author not defined` error | Add missing user to `authors.txt` and re-run |
| Clone hangs/times out | Use `--revision HEAD:1` to clone in reverse, or clone in chunks |
| Tags show as branches | Re-run the tag conversion script in Step 5 |
| Binary files corrupted | Check SVN `svn:mime-type` properties before migration |
| Large repo is slow | Use `svn2git` tool as an alternative to `git svn` |

---

> **💡 Tip:** Keep the SVN repo alive (read-only) for **30–60 days** as a reference before decommissioning.

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🧑‍💼 Incomplete Author Mapping
**What goes wrong:** Any SVN username missing from `authors.txt` causes the clone to **halt mid-migration**, forcing a restart.

**Impact:** Wasted hours, missed timeline.

**Mitigation:**
```bash
# Validate authors file is complete BEFORE cloning
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet \
  | grep "^r" | awk '{print $3}' \
  | sort -u > all_authors.txt
# Manually confirm every name has a Git identity mapped
```

---

### 2. 🌿 Branch & Tag History Loss
**What goes wrong:** SVN branches/tags are folders, not first-class objects. Merges and copies often **don't translate cleanly** to Git, resulting in orphaned or missing history.

**Impact:** Corrupted project history that is hard to fix after the team has started committing.

**Mitigation:**
- Audit `git log --all --graph` immediately after clone
- Spot-check 2–3 known branches against SVN history before pushing

---

### 3. ⏰ SVN Commit Freeze Violations
**What goes wrong:** A developer commits to SVN **during migration**, causing the Git copy to be out of sync the moment it's pushed.

**Impact:** Lost commits, manual reconciliation, or a full re-migration.

**Mitigation:**
- Enforce the pre-commit read-only hook **before** starting the clone
- Confirm with the whole team — not just developers (check CI bots, scripts, scheduled jobs)

---

> **Bottom line:** Author mapping breaks the process, branch loss corrupts history, and freeze violations invalidate the result. All three are **preventable with preparation done the night before.**

## Pre-Migration Checklist

- [ ] Freeze SVN commits (including CI bots & scheduled jobs)
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository
- [ ] Extract and verify **all** authors are mapped in `authors.txt`
- [ ] Audit branch/tag structure before cloning
- [ ] Validate commit counts and spot-check history after clone
- [ ] Set SVN to read-only before team cutover

If the migration fails or history is corrupted, **re-enable the SVN pre-commit hook and direct the team back to SVN** while you restart the migration from the backup dump.

```bash
# Restore SVN from backup
svnadmin load /path/to/svn/repo < svn_backup.dump
```

> This works because SVN was never deleted — only set to read-only.

**Git SVN must be installed** on the machine running the migration.

```bash
# Verify it's available
git svn --version
```

> Without this, the `git svn clone` command will fail immediately and nothing can proceed.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
**Compare commit counts** between SVN and Git.

```bash
# SVN count
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet | grep "^r" | wc -l

# Git count
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

> Takes seconds and immediately confirms whether history was fully transferred. If the numbers don't match, something went wrong before pushing anything.
**Morning:** Prep & author mapping → **Midday:** Clone & convert → **Afternoon:** Validate & push → **End of day:** Team cutover & SVN locked.

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
1. **`git svn`** — built into Git; handles the core SVN-to-Git clone and branch/tag conversion.
2. **`svn2git`** — a wrapper tool that automates and simplifies the full migration, including branch and tag cleanup.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text: The **project or team lead** should approve the final cutover, confirming that history is validated, all developers are notified, and CI/CD pipelines are updated before SVN is locked.
Send a single team-wide message **the day before** with the exact freeze time, the new Git repo URL, and the clone command ready to copy-paste — so no one has an excuse to be unprepared.

## Final Recap

| Phase | Key Action |
|---|---|
| **Prep** | Back up SVN, map all authors, freeze commits |
| **Migration** | Clone with `git svn`, convert branches and tags |
| **Validation** | Compare commit counts, spot-check history |
| **Cutover** | Push to Git, lock SVN, update CI/CD |
| **Communication** | Notify team the day before with clone command ready |

**Top 3 risks:** Author mapping gaps, branch/tag history loss, freeze violations.

**Rollback:** Restore SVN from backup dump and re-enable commits.

**Approval:** Team or project lead signs off before SVN is locked.

> Migration done right takes one focused day — the preparation the night before is what makes or breaks it.

- Prep the night before — backup, authors file, commit freeze
- Migrate midday using `git svn clone`
- Validate with commit count comparison
- Team lead approves cutover
- Push to Git, lock SVN, update CI/CD
- Rollback via SVN backup dump if needed
